The polynomial identity $T^9=T^8$ implies, on each eigenvector,
\[
0=(T^9-T^8)e_j=(\lambda_j^9-\lambda_j^8)e_j
=\lambda_j^8(\lambda_j-1)e_j.
\]
Since $e_j\ne0$, we have $\lambda_j^8(\lambda_j-1)=0$. Over $\mathbb C$, this yields $\lambda_j=0$ or $\lambda_j=1$.

Thus $T$ is diagonal in an orthonormal basis with only real diagonal entries. Consequently its adjoint is represented in the same basis by the same diagonal matrix, and therefore $T^*=T$.

For every basis vector,
\[
(T^2-T)e_j=(\lambda_j^2-\lambda_j)e_j=0,
\]
again because $\lambda_j\in\{0,1\}$. Hence $T^2-T$ vanishes on a basis, so $T^2=T$.
\end{proof}
